title: langchain pipeline vram usage when loading model
answer:
The vram usage of the langchain pipeline can be optimized by reducing the batch size and the maximum length of the input text. This can be achieved by setting the `batch_size` and `max_length` parameters in the `pipeline` function to smaller values. Additionally, you can try to use the `device` parameter to specify the GPU device to use, and make sure that the GPU device has enough memory to handle the model. You can also try to use the `torch.cuda.set_device` function to set the GPU device to use, and make sure that the GPU device is properly initialized before running the pipeline. Here is an example of how you can modify your code to optimize the vram usage:

``
pipe = pipeline(
    "text-generation",
    model=base_model,
    tokenizer=tokenizer,
    batch_size=1,
    device=0,
    max_length=50,
    temperature=0.6,
    top_p=0.95,
    repetition_penalty=1.2
)
```

You can also try to use the `torch.cuda.empty_cache` function to clear the GPU cache before running the pipeline, and the `torch.cuda.set_device` function to set the GPU device to use. Here is an example of how you can modify your code to use the GPU device and clear the GPU cache:

``
import torch

torch.cuda.set_device(0)

pipe = pipeline(
    "text-generation",
    model=base_model,
    tokenizer=tokenizer,
    batch_size=1,
    device=0,
    max_length=50,
    temperature=0.6,
    top_p=0.95,
    repetition_penalty=1.2
)

torch.cuda.empty_cache()
```

It is also recommended to check the documentation of the `langchain` library to see if there are any specific recommendations for optimizing vram usage.
